exercises.title: Interpret an alert

statement.title: The problem
paragraphs: Of 1,000 messages, 200 are urgent and 800 are nonurgent. An alert flags 80% of urgent messages and 10% of nonurgent messages. What fraction of flagged messages are urgent? Explain why the answer is not 80%.

parts: Compute how many messages of each type are flagged.
Use the flagged population to form the required fraction.
objectives: Distinguish a likelihood from the reversed conditional.

prerequisites.explanation: A conditional probability restricts the denominator to the group being conditioned on.

steps.purpose: Choose the conditioned population before dividing.
steps.prompt: How many messages are flagged altogether?

check.feedback: Count flagged urgent and flagged nonurgent messages; both belong in this population.

hints: Which group does “of flagged messages” restrict us to?
Compute each flagged subgroup, then add them.
steps.explanation: 160 urgent and 80 nonurgent messages are flagged, giving 240.

steps.purpose: Avoid reversing the conditional by comparing actual group counts.
steps.prompt: Explain the fraction of flagged messages that are urgent. Paper work is fine.

rubric: Uses all 240 flagged messages as the denominator.
Distinguishes urgent given flagged from flagged given urgent.

model_answer.title: Model answer
paragraphs: 160/240 = 2/3. The 80% rate is P(flagged | urgent), not P(urgent | flagged).

hints: The numerator is the intersection; the denominator is the conditioned group.
steps.explanation: The group after “given” determines the denominator.

blocks.title: Fraction of flagged messages that are urgent
paragraphs: P(urgent | flagged) = 160 / (160 + 80) = 2/3. It is not 80%, because nonurgent messages are four times as common, so they contribute half as many flags as urgent ones.

transfer.prompt: Now only 20 of the same 1,000 messages are urgent; both alert rates stay unchanged. Is the fraction of flagged messages that are urgent still 2/3?

answer.title: Answer
paragraphs: No. There are 16 flagged urgent and 98 flagged nonurgent messages, so the fraction is 16/114 = 8/57. The changed base rate matters.
